title: Open future, supervaluationism and the growing-block theory: a stage-theoretical account
version: Synthese 199(5–6), 14249–14266 (2021); online 11 November 2021; corrected publication 2022; DOI 10.1007/s11229-021-03419-7; PMCID PMC8581605
locator: Original PMC HTML: Introduction and GB formalization, lines 68–93; stage domains and strict growth condition (D), §2.2, lines 147–168; stage-relative F/P and quantifier clauses, §2.3, lines 169–182; quantifier troubles and rigid Σ_T diagnosis, §3, lines 196–222; shifting-timeline repair and 𝓔 clause, lines 223–245; conclusion lines 243–245; footnote 17 lines 304–305.
assumptions: Growing-block framework; stages are possible growth stages, domains expand along R, stage-history semantics; the paper adopts rather than defends the gappy supervaluationist treatment and does not offer a reductive account of stage-talk.
conclusion: Author argues that stage-theoretic interpretation of supervaluationism can express growing-block ontology and avoid the quantifier problem he attributes to Briggs and Forbes's fixed-timeline quantifier. The present report independently reconstructs the quantifier-parameter issue in a finite one-history model.
proof_status: Selected full-text inspection of the clauses and target sections; no complete proof audit and no independent reconstruction of the full Briggs–Forbes semantics.
dependencies: Thomason 1970 branching-time supervaluationist semantics (as used by Loss)
Briggs and Forbes 2012 growing-block supervaluationist account (as reconstructed and criticized by Loss, §3; not independently audited here)
open_questions: Does a branching stage semantics with a finite terminal branch preserve the intended growing-block axioms, or must only nonterminal stages be admitted?
How should domain-sensitive quantification and stage shifts be adapted to relativistic partial orders without a preferred global stage-history?
Which parts of Loss's diagnosis depend on the reconstructed Briggs–Forbes quantifier clauses, and how do they compare with the full original chapter?
relevance: Primary source for the exact frozen timeline / shifting stage domain problem and proposed repair.
limits: Toy model is a simplification, not a reproduction of every source clause. The semantic result does not establish ontology, truthmaking, bivalence/gaps, or relativistic application.
